newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kiev to shut Chernobyl reactor, one still works.
newsitem.headline: Kiev to shut Chernobyl reactor, one still works.

text.p: Ukraine will close one of two working reactors at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant on Saturday, taking a big step towards meeting promises to shut the site of the world's worst nuclear accident by the year 2000.
"Reactor number one is working at half capacity right now, but we will not reduce capacity gradually," said Yuri Neretin, the station's chief duty officer.

"At 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) the reactor will be simply switched off. Then there will be a period for the reactor to cool down and experts will investigate its condition. Later all the nuclear fuel will be removed."

Ukraine has promised to close the entire Chernobyl station by 2000 in exchange for some $3.1 billion in grants and credits from the Group of Seven industrialised states and President Leonid Kuchma said in April one reactor would close this year.

But industry officials have criticised the move and, worried about the problems of providing the former Soviet republic with electricity during the winter, have drawn up contingency plans to reopen the second reactor at the site.

Reactor number two was closed after a fire in the control room in 1991. The fourth reactor exploded in 1986, sending a radioactive cloud across much of Europe and its ruins are buried in a concrete sarcophagus, which is itself in need of repair.
Neretin said the onset of winter meant the timing for closing reactor number one was not ideal. Power cuts are already common in evening peak hours in rural areas during the winter.
Some industry experts have said that leaving Chernobyl with only one working reactor, number 3, could also cause problems.
They say it could be hard to keep water in the station's cooling system warm to prevent pipes from breaking if the single operating reactor was closed for repairs or after an accident.
"It is extremely dangerous to have only one reactor working in the winter," Ukraine's top Chernobyl negotiator, Yuri Kostenko, said earlier this month.
Nuclear officials have said the reactor to be closed on Saturday could be brought back on stream at any time. But Kuchma said on Friday there were no firm plans to reopen it.
"We would need hundreds and hundreds of million of dollars to rebuild it," he said. "The state does not have these funds."
The Chernobyl power station, one of five nuclear power plants in Ukraine, currently produces around five percent of the country's electricity.
The whole nuclear sector accounts for 40 percent of Ukraine's electricity in summer and 50 percent in winter.
Asked about the mood among Chernobyl's more than 5,000 employees, Neretin said:
"Why do you ask about mood? We are putting a brave face on it. But in all honesty we feel something like depression and don't want even to think about our future."
